title: Secrets of Strixhaven: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: As the giant shadow loomed, the Forum of Amity fell silent for the first time in its history.
Even as most archaics raged across Arcavios, others seemed to sink into contemplation.
Ajani no longer wanted to swing his axe in battle, but nothing came easier to him than defending those who needed protection.
Raising spirits is easier than taming them.
You can always tell who just left Professor Osgir's lecture on practical restoration.
"I checked my pack twice before we left campus. So why do I feel like I forgot something?"
Sharrel poured his heart into his words and watched them take flight.
"Our lives are built upon our pasts. What happens, then, if we are cut off from them?" —Augusta, dean of order
Not a journey's end but its beginning.
"Never be afraid to ask for help. Success is much sweeter when it's shared." —Quintorius Kand
"I'd start from scratch if I were you." —Felisa, Silverquill graduate
"My inklings are ideal for gathering information. There's no place on Arcavios they can't reach."
Silverquill professors dislike when students disrupt their lessons, but can't help approving of the confidence needed to do so.
Witnessing something firsthand is somehow both the best and the worst way to learn.
"I make promises, not threats."
"Of course I talk to myself. Who wouldn't want to hear me speak?"
"Just because Extus is gone doesn't mean the rest of us disappeared. We are here, and we are still seeking answers."
"Pranticle Peak is where you get the best views *on land*. I've found an even better vantage!"
"And I won't be writing any more essays for you, either!"
Though not all her students have wings, she's determined to help them reach new heights.
"For those who might consider cheating, its eyes can see everything. That includes you, Esme. Please see me after class." —Professor Ghostforge
The camel had traveled this route so often in life that its spirit began moving as soon as the mage finished the summoning.
One simple push and Jadzi fell into the churning swirl of magic. Tam thought it would be harder—wished that it had been harder.
"You're the one who brought a priceless scroll to a duel!"
Nothing gets in the way of a Prismari student following a great idea.
As Quandrix students advance in their studies, even slight miscalculations can have startling effects.
"Venturing beyond campus means learning how to deal with creatures not bound by university rules." —Emil, Vastlands roamer
"Dear dad, please send sixteen tons of krill in your next care package. Will explain at semester break."
"Return your lizards to their natural size before class ends. We don't want another incident." —Professor Berta
"We know you're working hard. Dress warm and get enough sleep. Dad says hi!" —Love, Mom
Only when they can defy the laws of nature can a Quandrix student claim to have mastered a spell.
The harder a foe strikes, the stronger a Dragonsguard's defenses become.
"Failure can be a reason to quit or fuel for inspiration. The choice is always yours." —Veyran, dean of perfection
Many Prismari students find their best ideas while under the gaze of the Muse.
Orysa and her troupe of turtles are a staple of Summitfest's daytime celebrations.
"To the patient mind, no problem is unsolvable."
"None of these projects are due until end of semester. I've still got a whole week to finish them!"
"Even the most familiar formulae can yield unexpected outcomes." —Professor Ruxa
The skycoach waits for no one.
Lluwen suddenly felt that he was seeing something very dangerous. The crackling magic, the thunderous chanting—the urge to turn and run replaced all his curiosity.
"My lovelies need meat, just like any other carnivore."
In most colleges, Erren's poisonous skin would have made them a pariah. In Witherbloom, they were one of the most popular students on campus.
"There will be moments when you are exhausted, with nothing left to give. Remember them when you finally succeed." —Embrose, dean of shadow
From the very first incision, Enid regretted choosing Witherbloom for her intercollege elective.
Just because the Oriq have gone silent doesn't mean their Mage Hunters have vanished.
She was entering her fiftieth year of graduate study with no signs of stopping.
"There are some lessons so simple that I thought they needn't be taught. I suppose I was wrong." —Moseo, dean of the vein
She had watched many arguments wither on the Forum floor. Now, it was time to call on them to prove her point.
"A reminder, students, that those of you unlucky enough to have lungs must mask up for this assignment." —Moseo, dean of the vein
"I expected better from you."
"Hold your applause. I am not yet finished."
"We celebrate our sadness because it reminds us of the true value of being alive."
"Does this taste like hemlock to you?"
The darkest corners of the Detention Bog hide natural laboratories that quietly spawn deadly infections.
"A little bruised, a little broken, but at least no longer dead." —Dina
"Let me guess, the scurrids got to you lot?" —Witherbloom infirmary attendant
Dara couldn't cover her Silverquill bullies in ink but she could do the next best thing.
"The whole display was uninspired and derivative, and left me wondering: what was the point?" — *Strixhaven Star* gallery show review
In the wake of the archaics' rampage, much worse was to come.
"This one's from my private stock."
"This place may be the Titan's Grave, but if you aren't careful it can be yours as well." —Professor Dellian Fel
Although lumarets are small magical creatures, they can gather to eliminate larger threats.
An incautious Lorehold student may learn more about the unbound rage of the Blood Age than they wanted to.
Its past became present became paradox.
His spirit has led this charge for centuries, unaware—or perhaps uncaring—of the way the fields have changed.
"My trick? Hit their casting hand and they lose their advantage. So far, I'm undefeated." —Alessia, Lorehold duelist
"Now, let your movements respond to the music! Yes, just like that!" —Introduction to Interpretation
Quintorius found that every new discovery motivated him to keep exploring.
"I don't care that they're 'off-limits,' the Lost Barracks hold too many war relics to not pay them a visit!"
"I don't want to hurt you, Ajani, but whatever Jace is planning needs to be stopped!"
Strixhaven students have a sense of humor. The spirits of the Blood Age do not.
Experience is a harsh tutor.
"My media? Fury and flame."
"Terrible creatures. A restorer's worst enemy is fire." —Osgir, the Reconstructor
"History is patient. I am not."
The annual arts festival, Summitfest, draws participants from across Arcavios, but only one will walk away with The Grand Muse trophy.
Leaving no stone unturned is just the beginning.
"Let's paint the field red!"
"You're history."
"He said it was 'physically impossible' to capture an exact likeness. The technique could use a little work, but I got the expression right." —Isobel, hot-headed artist
"Sometimes the only way to learn from history is by repeating it."
"What is the equation for terror?" —Lost research note, Paradox Gardens
"Numbers have no limits. Why should nature?" —Emil, Quandrix fourth-year
"I had to leave Doradur to attend Strixhaven, so I brought a piece of home with me."
"Scurrids to climb the tower, cervins to cross the stadium, and turtles to win the game." —Quandrix Mage Tower tactics
"Wherever your foot falls, life blossoms in its wake." —Lisette, dean of the root
"Now to put into practice what I learned in class."
The nature of the Paradox Gardens is such that the beasts that live there are always exactly as tall as they need to be to get a snack.
Though the lumarets were ignored by the other Witherbloom students, it was clear to Lluwen they were much more complex than they seemed.
"I sometimes think I've learned more from the smallest of beings than from all of my professors combined."
Brightly-colored skin doesn't always mean a creature is poisonous, but why take the risk?
Though the archaic had ravaged Titan's Grave and stolen Jadzi from safety, her compassion soothed its frenzy.
The sloths of Titan's Grave move so infrequently that entire ecosystems develop in their fur.
"Pests really live up to their name!" —Annia, disgruntled Ribtruss Town merchant
"Yes, she is blocking the path. Are you volunteering to move her?" —Tam, to Kirol
"Archaics and mana snarls have both existed since the beginning of time. Coincidence? Highly unlikely." —Zimone
"Potential can be augmented. Imagination cannot."
"Before we can understand nature, we must learn to nurture it."
"Life is vivid; the pigments I use should be too."
"Good play, team! Now let's run it again until it's perfect!"
Despite Blex's passing, Witherbloom students still continued the tradition of a yearly search in his honor. His son, however, took little effort to find.
"You will hear rumors that licking lumarets grants prophetic visions. That is untrue. Please refrain from licking the lumarets." —Witherbloom student handbook
"Professor, we study history and my neighbor wrote his answer first. I was learning from the past."
Prismari students are never afraid to let their imaginations run wild.
It's chaotic in the midst of the swarm—only when you step back does the pattern emerge.
"This last step is very important. You'll need to know if the friend you're searching for is alive or dead."
It soars in the presence of true beauty.
"Every lecture you attended—every theorem you memorized and equation you solved—has led to this first step into uncertainty." —Professor Deekah
"Life and death is a complex pattern that needs careful stitching."
The nature of theory given form and function.
"Creatures that have survived blood-soaked millennia should not be underestimated." —Nev, dean of substance
Not until Lluwen watched Professor Fel in action did he truly understand just how closely life and death were intertwined.
"There is no force stronger or more daunting than that of exponential growth."
"Do you think I've spent a lifetime studying war and learned nothing?"
"It's not ego if you're flawless, darling."
At the ready when words fail.
"Don't hold back, because I certainly won't."
"What the mind conceives," began Dean Adrix. "Magic can achieve," assured Dean Nev.
The best ideas stem from dreams.
It's characteristic of the Blood Age for instruments of music to also be tools of war.
The archaics experience all of Arcavian history. Changing that fate threatens their very existence.
"Here is my most important lesson: Within all life dwells a living essence. You must decide for yourselves how you'll use that knowledge." —Professor Longbranch
Hungering for the zest of life.
"Every weapon has a story. Let me tell you this one's."
Only proctors are allowed to use magic in exam halls, enabling them to more easily catch cheaters in the act.
"Be careful when traversing the Paradox Gardens. Not all experiments are perfectly contained." —Professor Berta
"Stones in your path are not obstacles, but discoveries." —Velomachus Lorehold
Fireworks of all kinds fill the skies of Summitfest.
"Seems like I took the words right out of your mouth."
School styluses are just tools. Passion is a Prismari's true instrument.
"Nature endures and adapts, and so shall we."
Eavesdropping is not a misdeed in the Forum, but a fact of life.
"Sorry. This seat's taken."
Rootha was humbled in the whale's presence. It was glorious and beautiful, all on its own terms.
Unflagging, unafraid, and undaunted.
The Prismari team takes the direction to "flood the zone" literally.
"Should your sloth become agitated, remove all valuables from the immediate area and wait for it to tire out. This will not take long." —Lorehold student handbook
"Speak as though the world will be a better place after your words are in it."
Krelg's attempt at a calming nap proved futile.
"Stop playing dead, Rinata. No one's believed you for a decade." —Moseo, dean of the vein
"I'll show you a 'colorful insult'!"
Choreography powers the spell, but improvisation shapes it.
"'It'll be fun,' they said. 'The Fields are full of dead things,' they said."
"Due dates are firm, and will be enforced."
"We make art. Art makes us." —Galazeth Prismari
Incapable of choosing a favorite and invulnerable to the influence of magic, it is an ideal and obnoxiously accurate referee.
The shops of Ribtruss Town sell anything that can be gathered within Titan's Grave. Just don't ask where they acquired their goods.
"Life is defined by change. When I shucked my flesh to combat the Phyrexian infection, it was not loss to me, merely a new state of being." —Moseo, dean of the vein
"Nature is chaos governed by principle. In analyzing these patterns, I hope to protect Strixhaven's future from any more tragedy." —Adrix, dean of theory
The terrible Blood Age lives on in the unending battle between thousands of spirits trapped in their final moments.
A sprawling edifice dedicated to promoting and protecting the fragile peace that holds Arcavios together.
A vast expanse that alters the rules of nature, offering a glimpse into the very structure of reality.
"The most cordial words are often the ones intended to deceive. It's only of late that I've realized how much strength honesty requires." —Embrose, dean of shadow
"Do you have all your books? And your stylus? And your extra uniform? And your lucky scarf?" —Overheard at Hookiver Station
Shaped by both its own wild nature and the magic of visiting artists, the Muse and the surrounding landscape are a wonder to behold.
"Careful ideation crashes together with wild creativity. Though I am grateful to be made dean, I've found it difficult to represent just the one side." —Veyran, dean of perfection
"Study of the past is preparation for the future. My fail-safe spell, activated upon my death, was precaution born from tales of the careless." —Augusta, dean of order
Some say this snarl—the most turbulent, changeable location in all of Arcavios—is the birthplace of the five elder dragons. There are also whispers it's where they are destined to die.
From the scattered skeleton of an ancient death grow the secrets of healing and prolonging life—or quietly ending it.
By himself, Lluwen couldn't have hoped to calm the Dawning Archaic—but any time it really mattered, he was never alone.
"Dangerously overflowing with creative expression." —*Strixhaven Star* gallery show review
"Theory? Meet practice." —Tam, Quandrix second-year
"If you take the time to listen, the archaics will tell you that this world has been torn asunder and remade many times before." —Jadzi, Oracle of Arcavios
In the grief that followed the Invasion, Willowdusk's office turned into an unofficial hideaway for overwhelmed students.
"All growth comes at a cost. It's up to each of us to determine if the result is worth the sacrifice." —Oracle Jadzi, to Tam
"I know the prompt was to replicate a scurrid, but I took some creative liberties with my version."
Few relics survived the turmoil of the Blood Age; those that did are powerful, dangerous, or both.
In the gloomy depths of Widdershins Hall sits an iron belly—always hungry, but generous to those who feed it.
"By all means, let's debate."
Two tired souls finally found something to unite them.
"What the mind conceives," began Dean Adrix. "Magic can achieve," assured Dean Nev.
As the marvels of living art they are, elemental whales can't resist contributing to Summitfest's displays.
"Knowledge is your armor. Use it wisely, and it will keep you safe." —Augusta, dean of order
"The *artist* should suffer for their craft, not the audience!" —Galazeth Prismari
So intense was their hatred they didn't realize how lonely they'd become. In the end, all they had was each other, and they hated that, too.
"Leave everything on the stage and give them a performance they'll never forget."
